title: Toll-takers earn 5 to 9 times the market's margin
dek: In Q2 FY27 IEX kept 84.6% of revenue as EBITDA, MCX 76.4% and NSE 75.7%; pallet pooler LEAP and Indus Towers about 55%. The median listed company kept 9.7%.

read: When revenue is a small fee on someone else's volume, margins stay high; the risk shifts to the fee itself, which a regulator or a large customer can reset.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Vantage business-model profiles

companies.name: Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd
National Stock Exchange of India Ltd

notes: EBITDA margin is EBITDA over revenue from operations in filed Q2 FY27 results (consolidated; Tips Music and LEAP standalone), so it can differ from company-reported figures: Indus Towers reports 54.4%, LEAP 50.8% on total income, and MCX cited 75% for H1 FY27. The market median covers 2,753 non-bank companies that filed Q2 FY27 results with EBITDA. How each earns comes from Vantage business-model profiles: IEX charges up to 2 paise per kWh per side, NSE ₹35.03 per ₹ lakh of equity option premium per side, Tips about ₹0.05 per YouTube stream, LEAP ₹1.54 per pallet per day (Q2 FY27). High margins do not mean high growth: IEX's revenue rose 8.6% and Indus Towers' 4.0% in Q2, against MCX's 113.7%. NSE's results are consolidated and include clearing.
